# Incident Report: MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.21.58 | Dominant local host in all conversations; source of all suspicious traffic |
| MAC | 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 | Consistent across ARP replies and Ethernet headers for 10.1.21.58 |
| Windows hostname | **WIN11OFFICE** (current NetBIOS name) | NBNS name registrations `WIN11OFFICE<00>`/`<1e>` broadcast from 10.1.21.58. Note: DHCP request and AD `_ldap._tcp` SRV lookups still reference **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** — this is the machine's original auto-generated Windows 11 name, seen in the DHCP hostname option and cached AD DNS records; the box was renamed to WIN11OFFICE locally but the rename had not fully propagated to AD/DHCP at capture time. Both names belong to the same MAC. |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 10.1.21.58 and the DC (10.1.21.2) |

## Malware Family

**Not signature-confirmed.** No file was recoverable from the capture: the entire payload transfer was TLS 1.3 with Encrypted Client Hello (SNI shown as the placeholder `cloudflare-ech.com`), so no HTTP headers, filename, Content-Disposition, or file hash could be extracted. No YARA/string match or plaintext binary was observed.

**Attribution: behavioral.** The traffic pattern is that of a **malvertising fake-file-download loader with a browser-fingerprinting gate**, consistent with pay-per-install/stealer-distribution infrastructure:

1. **t=45.3s** — DNS query for `hiyter.com`, immediately followed by
2. **t=45.8s** — DNS query and TLS session to `media.megafilehub4.lat` (104.21.48.156) — a fake file-hosting "download" landing page (Cloudflare-fronted, typosquat-style name mimicking legitimate mega-file-host branding)
3. **t=48.3s** — DNS query for `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67), immediately followed by a **16 MB encrypted transfer to the victim over 22.4 seconds** (frames 2776–~7000+, TLS 1.3/ECH) — this is almost certainly the malicious payload disguised as a downloaded file
4. **~20 second gap** (consistent with payload execution/installation)
5. **t=90.3s–118.5s** — the host begins repeated HTTP/HTTPS check-ins to `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49), `whooptm.cyou` (62.72.32.156), then `holiday-forever.cc` (80.97.160.24) and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (104.21.9.36) at t=123s/126s. All of this activity is confined to an 83-second burst; no recurrence anywhere else in the ~624-second capture (i.e., a single infection/check-in burst, not sustained beaconing).

The `whitepepper.su` traffic (plaintext HTTP, TCP stream 99) is a clear fingerprinting/telemetry gate: repeated `GET`/`POST /api/set_agent?id=<GUID>&token=<hex>&agent=Chrome|Edge&act=log` requests, with the POST body containing a full browser environment fingerprint (WebGL vendor/renderer, canvas fingerprint image, installed fonts, screen geometry, hardware concurrency, plugin list) — harvested from both an installed Chrome and an installed Edge profile on the victim. This is the signature behavior of a fingerprint/anti-sandbox gate used to vet infected hosts before further payload delivery, typical of stealer/loader PPI (pay-per-install) ecosystems.

TLS client fingerprinting supports this: the ClientHello JA3 hash `2800f914a7a4ba98aa9df62d316a460c` (and `68b3ecfaf0034bb9fcbecd518b5ab8d4`) recurs identically across the HTTPS connections to `whitepepper.su`, `whooptm.cyou`, `communicationfirewall-security.cc`, and `holiday-forever.cc` — distinct from the JA3 used for the initial browser-driven payload download (`09cc8725fe30ac191df5cf6b3365f528`) and from the genuine Chrome/Edge JA3s also seen talking to `whitepepper.su`. This indicates the four check-in domains were contacted by a single non-browser process (the dropped payload/loader itself), separate from the victim's real browsers.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / gate endpoints:**
- `153.92.1.49:80` — whitepepper.su, HTTP fingerprint-exfil gate (`/api/set_agent`, TCP stream 99, frames 24500–25303)
- `153.92.1.49:443` — whitepepper.su, TLS check-ins, JA3 2800f914a7a4ba98aa9df62d316a460c
- `62.72.32.156:443` — whooptm.cyou, TLS check-in at t=90.4s, same JA3 as whitepepper.su
- `80.97.160.24:443` — holiday-forever.cc, TLS check-in at t=122.8s
- `104.21.9.36:443` — communicationfirewall-security.cc, TLS check-ins at t=126.5s/127.7s
- `104.21.46.67:443` — arch.filemegahab4.sbs, payload delivery host (16 MB transferred, TLS 1.3/ECH)

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49)
- `whooptm.cyou` (62.72.32.156)
- `holiday-forever.cc` (80.97.160.24)
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (104.21.9.36, 172.67.141.109)
- `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13) — payload host
- `media.megafilehub4.lat` (104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67) — fake download landing page
- `hiyter.com` (104.21.22.231, 172.67.207.145) — pre-landing-page redirector, queried immediately before megafilehub4.lat

**URLs:**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome` (frame 24500)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (frame 24601, POST — browser fingerprint exfil)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log` (frame 25286, same GUID/token, second browser profile)

**Files:** none recoverable. The payload transfer from arch.filemegahab4.sbs was fully encrypted (TLS 1.3, ECH-concealed SNI) with no cleartext headers, so no filename or SHA256 could be extracted from the capture.

**Benign context (not IOCs):** Windows NCSI (`www.msftconnecttest.com`, `dns.msftncsi.com`), Microsoft/Office/Skype telemetry (`*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `config.edge.skype.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`), MSN/Bing (`www.msn.com`, `www.bing.com`, `th.bing.com`), Google services (`accounts.google.com`, `clients*.google.com`, `*.googleapis.com`, `safebrowsing.google.com`), internal AD/DC traffic (Kerberos, LDAP, DCE-RPC/SAMR/LSARPC to 10.1.21.2), SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR/NBNS local broadcast noise, and repeated WPAD lookups (all NXDOMAIN, standard Windows behavior).
